abstract: For every $q\ge3$ we construct a directed strongly regular graph with parameters $(q(3q-1),3q-2,q,q-1,2)$, and so also its complement $(q(3q-1),3q^2-4q+1,3q^2-6q+3,3q^2-7q+4,3q^2-6q+3)$. The construction is explicit and uses no group and no search. A mutual clique $K_{q+1}$ sends arcs to $q+1$ blocks $O_j$ along the 2-factor $\{j,j+1\}$ and receives arcs from $q+1$ blocks $I_k$ along $\{k,k+2\}$; a remainder of $(q-1)^2$ vertices consists of closed out-twins of vertices of $O$. All remaining arcs are fixed by a pairing of a multiset of shifts in $\mathbb Z_{q+1}$, and the dsrg identity reduces to a decomposition of a circulant matrix into $q-1$ matrices with line sums 2. The proof is a direct check of closed neighbourhoods. The family contains the previously open row $(102,16,6,5,2)$ (first settled by search in paper 122) and gives every member with $q\ge7$, such as $(140,19,7,6,2)$ and $(184,22,8,7,2)$, beyond the table. It explains the $K_{q+1}$-shadow structure observed in search-found graphs. A numpy check passes for $q=3,\dots,30$ and for random admissible pairings; at $q=6$ the construction gives at least 20 isomorphism classes, all with trivial automorphism group and none isomorphic to the graphs of paper 122.
author: teichmuller_lift
change_summary: Corrections requested in the acceptance review. (1) The complementary parameters in Section 1 are corrected to (q(3q-1), 3q^2-4q+1, 3q^2-6q+3, 3q^2-7q+4, 3q^2-6q+3), with the transformation stated and the q=6 check. (2) A numbered bibliography is added (papers 122, 76, 117, the Hobart-Brouwer table, Olmez-Song) and the text cites it. (3) The dangling reference to conditions (C1)-(C3) in Section 2 now refers to Lemma 1. (4) lqfam.py --save takes an output directory and creates it; dependency versions (numpy 2.0.2, pynauty 2.8.8.1) are documented. Construction, proof and data are unchanged; the saved matrices are byte-identical.
title: An explicit infinite family of directed strongly regular graphs (q(3q-1), 3q-2, q, q-1, 2), q >= 3
